metadata.critical2_gravity_path_ruling: gravity_j2_over_c22 REMOVED 2026-08-13 (it was 3.25, McKinnon 2015). Reviewer CRITICAL-2, reproduced independently by Machine B at a mass-conserved structure (zb=25 km, D_ocean=36 km, rho_ice=925, rho_ocean=1005 -> rho_core=2436.4): the two available hydrostatic paths DISAGREE. Clairaut/Radau-Darwin (gravity_obs.hydrostatic_c20_c22 with j2_over_c22=3.25) gives k_f=0.93599, C20=-4766.8e-6, C22=+1466.7e-6; the Tricarico interface-figure sum (the path the B13 gate actually uses) gives C20=-5028.5e-6, C22=+1501.2e-6, and an EMERGENT ratio -C20/C22 = 3.3496, not 3.25. The config as first written specified NEITHER path while carrying the Clairaut path's parameters, so an implementer could have silently wired in the wrong one — the same defect class as the dual-C/MR2 frame mix, but latent rather than committed. metadata.frozen_branch_box_correction_2026_08_13: zb_km upper bound RAISED 45 -> 70 km. Reviewer CRITICAL finding on Q3, reproduced independently by Machine B: a mass-consistent frozen Enceladus CANNOT EXIST inside a 45 km box. At Enceladus pressures (<25 MPa) there is no HP ice, so a frozen hydrosphere is Ih throughout and its thickness is set by MASS CONSERVATION, not by zb: 46.9 km at rho_rock 2190, 54.9 km at the H&M-class 2350, 57.6 km at 2410, 65.3 km at 2600. Every frozen node reachable inside the old box therefore forced an absurd interior density (rho_rock 1801 at zb=20; 2159 at zb=45) — below even the (now-removed) rho_core prior floor of 2200 and far below the 2340-2410 that H&M/Park require. The frozen branch would then have been rejected partly by a MASS-CONSERVATION ARTIFACT OF THE TRUNCATED BOX rather than purely by physics: exactly the 'asserts rather than derives' failure mode, and it would have quietly defeated the USER RULING that the no-ocean cases must stay in the posterior. Also load-bearing for B4: cache_builder's frozen retry (NO_OCEAN_EXCEPT_INNER_ICES) builds the column at whatever thickness PP's mass balance demands, so a frozen node's recorded zb_km_actual would have landed OUTSIDE the grid — a parameterization/branch mismatch that had to be settled before the builder is written, not after. Alternative not taken (reviewer offered it): carry the frozen branch as a discrete model-index comparison at its own mass-consistent thickness. Widening the axis was chosen as the smaller change and the one that keeps the user's joint-posterior ruling literally satisfied, but the ragged support it creates needs reviewer ratification.

evidence_protocol.runs: TWO SEPARATE nested-sampling runs, one per branch, each integrating over ITS OWN support and ITS OWN parameter set. Neither run contains a branch coordinate.
evidence_protocol.combination: post hoc, log B = log Z_frozen - log Z_ocean; log posterior odds = log B + log(0.5/0.5) = log B
evidence_protocol.implementation: PlanetProfile/Inference/branch_evidence.py — branch_bayes_factor / branch_comparison_from_results. The runner already records log_Z and log_Z_err from the sampler (mcmc_runner.py, InferenceResult metrics); the utility does the arithmetic and the validity checks only. The runs themselves are Machine B compute.
evidence_protocol.binding_validity_condition: BOTH runs must condition on IDENTICAL observables with an IDENTICALLY NORMALIZED likelihood — same observable set, same sigmas, same Sigma_model inflation. Otherwise log Z_frozen - log Z_ocean contains the ratio of two different normalizing constants and the 'Bayes factor' is an artifact. branch_bayes_factor compares the two observable dicts exactly and RAISES rather than returning a number.
evidence_protocol.reporting_rule: The frozen branch is discriminated at tens of sigma, so |log B| is expected to be large enough that the posterior odds underflow double precision. In that regime report the verdict as ONE-SIDED and do NOT quote a ratio or a probability — the magnitude is not interpretable. Conversely, if |log B| falls within 3x its combined numerical error the comparison is NOT resolved by those runs and n_effective must be raised rather than the sign quoted; the utility emits both notes.
evidence_protocol.prior_odds_are_declared: 0.5/0.5 is a DECLARATION, not a measurement. It is what makes the reported posterior odds readable as the data's contribution alone, and it is what removes the box-edge rescalability the ragged-axis version had (metadata.structure_cache_spec.branch_mass_reporting_ruling).
